disclaimer: The backpack economy of the opt-in survival set (D-092): which Sophisticated Backpacks tiers and upgrades exist in Underground City, at what size, and why. Run scripts/generate_backpack_config.py to regenerate the Sophisticated server and common configuration (content/generated/survival-config/) and Core's copy of this policy (rpg-core/src/main/resources/data/underground_city/backpack_policy/policy.json). Core checks at every server start that the mod's recipes obey the policy and removes any disabled recipe it finds (BackpackPolicyEnforcer). The policy is convenience, not power: a backpack carries more, it does not produce, automate, repair or heal anything.

leatherBackpack.why: The everyday pack, sold in every city for 70 credits and craftable from leather, string and a chest: a newcomer carries a little more than their pockets within the first hour.

copperBackpack.why: Eight copper ingots around the basic pack. Worth it for a farmer or a smith who hauls goods; still one upgrade slot.

ironBackpack.why: Eight iron ingots. The working pack of a tradesperson: the player's own inventory plus one more, and a second upgrade slot.

goldBackpack.why: Eight gold ingots. More room, not more upgrades: the capacity of a delivery driver.

diamondBackpack.why: Eight diamonds. The most a person should carry without a vehicle; the upper end of what the economy is balanced around.

netheriteBackpack.why: A smithing upgrade with a netherite ingot (a trip to the Nether). The top tier is deliberately below the mod's default of 120 slots and 7 upgrades.

why.allowOpeningOtherPlayerBackpacks: Nobody can open the pack another player is wearing (the right-click route the mod offers): contents belong to the person carrying them.
why.itemFluidHandlerEnabled: The mod itself warns that the fluid handling of a backpack in item form can duplicate items or fluids together with other mods' tanks.
why.tickDedupeLogicDisabled: Stays false: the mod's periodic check that notices two packs with the same contents id (a copied item stack) and gives one of them a new, empty id, so a duplicated stack cannot duplicate the contents.
why.containerItemsDisallowed: No shulker boxes or other container items inside a pack (nesting would multiply capacity).
why.maxUpgradesPerStorage: One stack upgrade and one jukebox per pack, and no furnace upgrade: capacity multiplication and portable production stay small.
why.nerfs: Carrying more than two backpacks slows the player, and only the worn pack runs its automatic upgrades (magnet, pickup, feeding), so spare packs cannot be stacked into a vacuum cleaner.
why.entityBackpackAdditions: Mobs never spawn wearing backpacks with loot, and never drop them: a backpack is made or bought, never farmed from a monster (D-093).
why.magnetUpgrade: Three blocks: it picks up what you dropped at your feet, not the street.

common.why: No backpacks or upgrades in vanilla chests: loot would hand out upgrades the policy removed and would undercut the supplier.

enabled.why: The basic leather pack: 27 slots (a vanilla chest) and one upgrade slot. Recipe: 4 string, 4 leather and a wooden chest. Sold in every city so that a newcomer is never without one, and the base of every bigger pack.
Second tier, 36 slots and one upgrade slot: the basic pack ringed with 8 copper ingots (a branch beside the iron one).
Third tier, 45 slots and two upgrade slots: the basic pack ringed with 8 iron ingots. The first pack that carries a working loadout (one upgrade for pickup, one for feeding).
Fourth tier, 54 slots and two upgrade slots: the iron pack ringed with 8 gold ingots. A double chest of room, still only two upgrades.
Fifth tier, 72 slots and three upgrade slots: the gold pack ringed with 8 diamonds. A deliberate mid-game purchase of real materials.

Top tier, 90 slots and four upgrade slots: the diamond pack, a netherite ingot and a netherite upgrade template at a smithing table. Capped well below the mod default (120 slots, 7 upgrades) so that carrying never replaces storage and logistics.
